mlp.code:
def f(p):                                 # block 0's MLP on 4 tokens, as a function of its weights
    return mlp(p, x)                      # x: f32[4,128] -> f32[4,128]

y, f_lin = jax.linearize(f, p)            # primal output and the linear map p_dot -> y_dot
f_T = jax.linear_transpose(f_lin, p)      # the transposed map y_bar -> p_bar
_, f_vjp = jax.vjp(f, p)                  # what jax.grad uses: linearize, then transpose

    f:f32[4,512] = dot_general[
      dimension_numbers=(([1], [0]), ([], []))
      preferred_element_type=float32
    ] a c
    g:f32[1,512] = broadcast_in_dim[broadcast_dimensions=(1,)] b
    h:f32[4,512] = add f g
    i:f32[4,512] = mul 0.5:f32[] h
    j:f32[4,512] = neg h
    k:f32[4,512] = mul j 0.7071067690849304:f32[]
    l:f32[4,512] = erfc k
    m:f32[4,512] = mul i l
    n:f32[4,512] = copy m
    o:f32[4,128] = dot_general[
      dimension_numbers=(([1], [0]), ([], []))
      preferred_element_type=float32
    ] n e
    p:f32[1,128] = broadcast_in_dim[broadcast_dimensions=(1,)] d
    q:f32[4,128] = add o p
  in (q,) }
